The demand for labour is derived because:
options: It depends on the demand for the product that workers make
Workers choose how much to supply
questions.why: Firms want workers for the output they produce.

questions.q: A firm pays £80 a day. The MRP of the next worker is £95. A profit maximiser will:
questions.why: The worker adds £15 more to revenue than to costs.

questions.q: Which would shift the demand curve for labour to the LEFT?
options: A fall in demand for the product
A rise in the product's price
A rise in the price of capital that replaces labour
questions.why: Derived demand falls when demand for the product falls.

questions.q: Demand for labour is more elastic when machines can easily replace workers.
questions.why: A wage rise then leads firms to switch away from labour.

questions.q: Explain why a firm hires fewer workers at a higher wage.

ideas.label: MRP falls as more workers are hired, because of diminishing returns
The firm hires only while MRP is at least the wage

questions.model: Because of diminishing returns, MRP falls as more workers are hired. The firm hires only while MRP is at least equal to the wage, so a higher wage means fewer workers are worth hiring.
questions.why: Compare what the next worker adds with what they cost.

tests.answer: Diminishing returns mean MRP falls, and the firm only hires while MRP is at least the wage.
